attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own essay, given in first person.

semantics.note: 'I believe... will die' is a firm conditional forecast, not a hedge. The antecedent 'once the VC subsidies dry up' and the quantifier 'most' are kept. The data-center half of the sentence is rightly left out.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: more than half by count, with closure counting as death but acquisitions not. Requiring a sector-wide withdrawal first follows the antecedent. Continued funding is correctly not treated as a contradiction.

evidence.note: Crunchbase Q3 2026 global report showing strong AI and seed funding. It bears on the antecedent (not met), not on whether startups die, so it is context, not a contradiction.
Crunchbase North America Q3 2026 report: $61B to AI rounds. This shows the antecedent has not happened. It is not evidence about the conditional outcome.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm conditional forecast with no deadline. The packet shows VC funding for AI is still strong as of Q3 2026, so the antecedent (subsidies drying up) has not happened, and an unmet antecedent means the claim is not scored. No closure data for any cohort exists. The forecast stays open.

attribution.note: Zitron's own first-person statement in his essay.

semantics.note: 'I believe... have no future' is firm. But the normalised 'relies on' drops the exclusivity in 'only made possible through', which understates the revenue claim. The contract restores it. The sentence is a compound: an undated forecast plus a present-tense causal assertion.

contract.note: Reading the claim as business failure, not acquisition, is fair. So is treating the revenue clause as exclusive dependency, and so is not importing the VC antecedent. Using Q1 2026 as the revenue period is the evaluator's choice but reasonable, and it does not decide the result.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1 discloses customer concentration (top five about 25%) for Jan–Sep 2026. That is a different period and metric, and it says nothing about whether customers are subsidised or experimental. It is also a company disclosure.

reviews.rationale: The survival forecast has no deadline. Neither company has failed, and continued operation cannot refute an undated forecast. The packet has no customer-level evidence showing or disproving that revenue depends only on subsidised startups or experimental spending. Neither part is settled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words, with 'I believe' set in the middle of a firm 'will never' statement.

semantics.note: 'I believe... will never make even a quarter of their costs back' is a firm undated forecast. The $200B and 25% thresholds are kept. 'Assuming they ever turn on' is an intensifier, not a real antecedent.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: permanent failure before 25% of project costs are recovered, totalling at least $200B. Excluding temporary delays and transfers is fair. With no deadline, resolving against the claim needs a full terminal accounting, which is appropriate.

evidence.note: One unfinished Texas project went bankrupt in November 2025 and was later acquired for conversion to AI use. There are no cost or recovery figures, and it is far from the $200B threshold.
A secondary compilation of GPU credit stress, including the line 'no GPU-backed loan has been publicly foreclosed'. It covers compute credit, not project cost recovery.

reviews.rationale: This is an undated forecast. The packet shows isolated distress but no verified set of failed projects with costs and sub-25% recovery anywhere near $200B. Time passing without failures cannot contradict it. It remains open.

attribution.note: Zitron's own analysis of NVIDIA's investments and commitments.

semantics.note: Revision 2 keeps the scale, the named companies, the $30B figure and the six-year window. This is a present-tense description of existing commitments, so it is an observation. The superlative is rhetoric.

contract.note: The contract is fair, and it rightly excludes the dot-com superlative. The result turns on interpretations the speaker did not supply: whether 'investing' covers conditional rights and commitments, and whether a schedule ending 'FY2032 and thereafter' fits 'next six years'.

evidence.note: NVIDIA's 10-Q: $30B in cloud commitments, about $28B of it due by FY2031 and $2B in FY2032 and thereafter. This roughly matches six years. It also lists $27B in contingent investment commitments. But it says cloud deals mainly support R&D, which undercuts the customer-financing framing.
OpenAI's announcement of $30B from NVIDIA plus NVIDIA inference compute. This backs tens of billions in investment and a reciprocal tie. It is an announcement, not cash paid.
The IREN deal is a five-year conditional right to invest up to $2.1B, plus deployment of NVIDIA infrastructure. It shows reciprocity, but the investment is a right, not a completed investment.

reviews.rationale: Holds: the $30B cloud commitment (mostly due within about six fiscal years), tens of billions via OpenAI's $30B, and reciprocal product ties with OpenAI and IREN. Not established: CoreWeave and Anthropic have no evidence in the packet, IREN is only a conditional right, and NVIDIA says the cloud deals are mainly for R&D. That weakens the claim that it is paying customers to buy its products. The superlative is unscored rhetoric.
